title: Spoofed GCS heartbeats suppress the data-link-loss failsafe
description: PX4 accepts HEARTBEAT unsigned on every link and derives GCS liveness from MAV_TYPE_GCS heartbeats. While the real GCS link is jammed or down, an adversary who can deliver MAVLink to any FC link impersonates the GCS, so the data-link-loss failsafe (DD-05) never triggers and the vehicle flies on without C2 or automatic return. Residual after SR-001: a compromised CC or GCS, both already inside the C2 trust base.

title: Commands reach the FC outside the modeled C2 path
description: An enabled uXRCE-DDS client or an unused MAVLink instance (the px4_fmu-v6x defaults enable MAVLink on Ethernet) gives a peer a path to the FC that bypasses the CC. MAVLink signing does not cover uXRCE-DDS at all.

title: Privileged MAVLink services used to reconfigure the FC
description: A peer that can send signed MAVLink (any key holder, or a compromised CC or GCS) uses the MAVLink shell (SERIAL_CONTROL), MAVLink FTP or parameter writes to change failsafes, delete files or run commands on the FC. Residual: CC-originated commands and the USB maintenance link are not filtered.

title: Signed commands cannot be attributed to a key holder
description: All holders share one signing key, so the FC cannot tell whether the GCS, CC or MSS signed a command. MAVLink alone cannot show who issued it.

title: MAVLink flood on the CC-FC link degrades the FC
description: A malfunctioning or compromised CC process, or a tap on the UART, floods the FC with MAVLink traffic and starves message handling. Residual: a fully compromised CC can bypass the rate limit.

title: Memory-safety flaw in FC MAVLink handling exploited
description: Crafted MAVLink exploits a parsing flaw in PX4 and gains code execution on the FC. The MAVLink frame parser runs on unauthenticated input; the PX4 v1.17 release notes list MAVLink FTP path-traversal hardening, so flaws of this class occur.

title: Vehicle impersonated with a stolen CC WireGuard key
description: An adversary holding the CC's WireGuard private key, for example from a captured vehicle, poses as the vehicle to the GCS and feeds it false telemetry and video.

title: Persistent modification of CC software
description: An adversary with physical access, a malicious update or a foothold on the CC modifies its boot chain, root filesystem or configuration so the compromise survives reboot.

title: CC failure removes all C2
description: All C2 passes through the CC (DD-01), so a CC crash, hang or power fault cuts the vehicle off from the GCS.

title: Code execution on the CC yields full vehicle C2
description: An adversary who gains code execution on the CC, through a flaw in a network-facing or media service or a malicious peripheral, reads the shared signing key and signs any command to the FC. Top threat of the architecture (section 4.2). Residual: full CC compromise still yields C2, inherent to PX4's shared-key signing.

title: Tampered payload attacks the CC over USB
description: A payload with modified firmware enumerates as an unexpected USB device class, such as a keyboard or network adapter, to attack the CC.

title: Tampered or counterfeit navigation module
description: A GNSS or compass module with modified firmware, introduced through the supply chain or maintenance, reports false position or heading. Residual: a modification made before receipt that leaves the reported firmware version unchanged.

title: Tampered ESC firmware commands unsafe thrust
description: ESC firmware modified through the supply chain, or over DroneCAN by a compromised node, ignores or distorts FC commands.

title: Compromised air radio attacks the CC
description: An air radio compromised over RF or through its own firmware sits on the CC's Ethernet segment and attacks CC services directly.

title: Compromised ground radio attacks the GCS host
description: A ground radio compromised over RF or through its own firmware sits on the GCS host's network interface and attacks GCS services directly.

title: Stolen or unattended GCS used to command the vehicle
description: Someone with physical access to an unattended or stolen GCS laptop uses its keys and session to command the vehicle.

title: Tampered GCS software
description: A modified QGroundControl build or operating-system package, inserted upstream or during installation, forges commands or misreports telemetry while holding the signing key.

title: Operator actions cannot be attributed
description: Without a per-operator record, the GCS cannot show which operator issued a command.

title: Malware from unrelated use compromises the GCS
description: Email, web browsing, removable media or other networks used on the GCS deliver malware that obtains the signing and WireGuard keys.

title: Unauthorized use of the MSS
description: Someone with access to an unattended MSS uses it to load software or provision keys.

title: Build environment inserts malicious code into signed artifacts
description: A compromised build host or toolchain alters firmware or images before signing, so devices accept them as genuine.

title: Maintenance actions cannot be attributed
description: Without a per-maintainer record, the MSS cannot show who loaded software or provisioned keys.

title: MSS compromised through its online connection
description: The MSS fetches upstream sources (DF-16). Malware arriving that way gains access to master key material and to the maintenance links into the vehicle.

title: GNSS spoofing diverts the vehicle
description: Counterfeit civil GNSS signals shift the position estimate and steer the vehicle off its route or into a hazard. PX4 alerts on spoofing the receiver reports, and with EKF2_GPS_CHECK bit 9 set it also stops relying on that GNSS data. Residual: spoofing the receiver does not report goes unflagged.

title: Impersonated upstream source
description: A typosquatted package, a dependency-confusion name or a compromised mirror supplies code that appears to come from a legitimate project.

title: Signing key read from the FC's SD card
description: Anyone with brief physical access to the SD card copies the 40-byte key file and becomes a key holder. The key alone does not reach the FC over RF (SR-001), but it does over USB or a telemetry port.

title: Signing key file replaced or deleted
description: Replacing the key file installs an adversary's key and locks out the GCS. Deleting it disables signing on every link at the next boot.

title: Flight logs reveal mission areas and routes
description: ULogs on the SD card of a captured vehicle show where it flew and what it did.

title: Flight logs altered or deleted to hide activity
description: A peer with MAVLink FTP access edits or deletes ULogs remotely. Residual: anyone holding the SD card can do the same.

title: FC firmware or parameters modified through the bootloader or debug port
description: With physical access, an adversary flashes modified PX4 firmware over USB or rewrites flash over SWD.

title: Firmware and parameters extracted from a captured FC
description: An adversary reads the PX4 firmware image and parameter set from a captured FC.
acceptance_rationale: PX4 is open source and the parameter baseline is published in P1. The only secret on the FC is the signing key, covered by THR-026.

title: CC storage rewritten offline
description: An adversary removes or reflashes the CC's storage to replace the boot chain or root filesystem.

title: CC system image read from a captured vehicle
description: An adversary copies the CC's root filesystem and configuration from a captured vehicle.
acceptance_rationale: The image holds open-source software and configuration documented in P1 and P4. It contains no secrets; credentials are kept in DS-CC-CRED (THR-034).

title: Keys extracted from a captured CC
description: An adversary extracts the CC's copy of the signing key and its WireGuard private key from a captured vehicle.

title: CC trust anchors replaced
description: Replacing the stored GCS public key or signing key makes an adversary's GCS a trusted peer.

title: Imagery and mission plan read from a captured vehicle
description: Survey imagery and the active mission plan are read from the CC's storage.

title: Keys stolen from a lost or stolen GCS
description: The signing key and the GCS WireGuard private key are copied from the laptop's disk.

title: Mission plans and imagery disclosed from the GCS
description: Mission plans, telemetry logs and received imagery are read from the laptop's disk.

title: Master key material stolen from the MSS
description: The master signing key, WireGuard key pairs and software signing keys are copied from the MSS.

title: Software signing key lost
description: If the firmware signing private key is lost, devices that trust it can no longer be updated. PX4's secure-boot guide warns that recovery then needs a debug probe.

title: Release artifacts tampered before loading
description: Built images, firmware or SBOMs are modified in MSS storage between build and load.

title: Commands injected or altered over the RF uplink
description: An RF-proximate adversary injects or modifies commands, mission uploads or parameter writes on the air-ground link.

title: Commands and mission uploads read over RF
description: An RF-proximate adversary records the uplink and reads commands and flight plans.

title: RF jamming of the uplink
description: Jamming blocks the uplink. Residual: jamming itself cannot be prevented (A-12); the vehicle returns under the data-link-loss failsafe.

title: Spoofed telemetry misleads the operator
description: Forged or altered telemetry shows the operator a false vehicle state.

title: Telemetry read over RF
description: An RF-proximate adversary records the downlink and reads vehicle position and status.

title: RF emissions reveal vehicle and GCS locations
description: Transmissions reveal that the vehicle and GCS are operating, and direction finding locates them.
acceptance_rationale: WireGuard hides content, not the existence, timing or direction of transmissions. Emission control belongs to the waveform and EW, both out of scope (A-12).

title: Video intercepted over RF
description: An RF-proximate adversary records the downlink and recovers payload video.

title: Unsigned or forged frames injected on the CC-FC UART
description: A tap fitted to the UART injects frames. Signing rejects them unless the adversary holds the key, except for the four messages PX4 accepts unsigned.

title: Spoofed ADSB_VEHICLE or COLLISION messages
description: PX4 accepts both unsigned. Spoofed ADSB_VEHICLE reports drive traffic avoidance (NAV_TRAFF_AVOID); PX4 v1.18.0-rc1 has no receive handler for COLLISION. The system has no ADS-B receiver, so neither message has a legitimate source.

title: Spoofed RADIO_STATUS throttles FC telemetry
description: A spoofed RADIO_STATUS reporting a low transmit buffer cuts the FC's outgoing stream rate by 20% per message, down to 1%, when software throttling is active on that link. The IP radios send no RADIO_STATUS.

title: Tampered FC telemetry misleads CC autonomy
description: Altered or injected telemetry on the FC-to-CC link leads onboard autonomy to act on a false vehicle state.

title: Malformed imagery exploits the CC video pipeline
description: A tampered payload sends a crafted video stream that exploits a parsing flaw in the CC's media pipeline.

title: GNSS jamming denies position
description: Jamming removes or degrades GNSS. PX4 alerts on jamming the receiver reports, but treats it as a failed GNSS check only when EKF2_GPS_CHECK bit 11 is set, which is off by default. COM_POS_LOW_ACT (default Return) acts on low position accuracy only in mission or loiter modes.

title: False navigation data injected on the NAV-FC wiring
description: Someone with physical access to the airframe taps the navigation module's wiring and injects false position or heading.

title: Actuator commands altered on the FC-ESC wiring
description: Someone with physical access to the airframe taps the actuator wiring and alters motor commands.

title: Unauthorized peer installs the first signing key
description: Before a key exists, PX4 v1.18 accepts SETUP_SIGNING unsigned on any link. A peer that reaches any FC link first installs its own key and locks out the GCS until the SD card is cleared. Source: the v1.18 change that accepts SETUP_SIGNING on any link instead of USB only.

title: Unsigned firmware loaded through the USB bootloader
description: The PX4 bootloader accepts any firmware image over USB unless secure boot is enabled.

title: Malicious image or credentials loaded into the CC
description: A rogue maintenance device, or a compromised MSS, loads a modified image or replacement credentials over the maintenance link.

title: Keys exposed on removable media during GCS provisioning
description: Signing and WireGuard keys copied to removable media for the GCS can be lost, copied or left behind.

title: Crafted offload data exploits the MSS
description: A compromised CC returns crafted imagery or logs that exploit software on the MSS, the host with every key.

title: Crafted flight logs exploit MSS log tools
description: A tampered FC or SD card returns crafted ULogs that exploit log-analysis tools on the MSS.

title: Compromised upstream release enters the build
description: A malicious change in a legitimate upstream project or release (a PX4 submodule, a distribution package or a toolchain) is built into signed artifacts.

title: Flaw in PX4's signing implementation lets forged frames through
description: PX4 states its signing implementation has not been audited, and signing fixes are still landing: PR #28891 (forwarding of signed frames) merged on main on 2026-09-30, after the pinned v1.18.0-rc1. A remaining flaw could let a peer without the key pass signature checks.

title: Signed frames replayed after an FC reboot
description: PX4 notes the on-disk signing timestamp usually stays at its provisioning value, because vehicles are powered off without a graceful shutdown. Assumption, to be checked in VE-02: after a reboot, frames recorded since provisioning may pass the timestamp check. Over RF the adversary sees only WireGuard ciphertext, so recording needs a tap inside the vehicle or a key holder.
